item.title: China-EU consensus on vehicle trade to stabilize industry expectations: CAAM
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- The consensus reached between China and the European Union (EU) on hybrid and electric vehicle trade will help stabilize industry expectations on both sides and ensure the smooth operation of automotive industrial and supply chains, the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers (CAAM) said on Wednesday. The consensus follows intensive bilateral talks under the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, guided by the principles of mutual respect and equal consultation, the CAAM said in a statement. As major global economies and automotive markets, China and the EU have strong industrial complementarity and broad scope for cooperation, the association said. Managing differences and properly addressing trade frictions through institutionalized consultations, replacing confrontation with dialogue and resolving disputes through cooperation, are a rational choice that serves the fundamental interests of both sides, the CAAM noted. Escalating trade tensions would raise business costs, disrupt normal market order and harm consumers, while hindering the automotive industry's transformation and upgrading, the CAAM said. Regarding hybrid vehicles, the two sides emphasized and confirmed three basic principles: respect for facts, non-discrimination and compliance with World Trade Organization rules. On electric vehicles, China and the EU achieved a "soft landing" in the EU's anti-subsidy case in January this year, with the bloc issuing a general guidance document on price undertakings. The EU will continue to advance relevant procedures concerning price undertakings by companies involved in the case, as well as other review procedures. The consensus will provide a more predictable environment for automotive companies to pursue trade and investment cooperation and help safeguard the shared interests of industry players and consumers on both sides, the CAAM said. The association said it would continue to promote industry dialogue and coordination, support China and the EU in working together under their trade and investment consultation mechanism to implement the consensus and properly resolve differences, and jointly uphold a fair, open and non-discriminatory international trading environment. ■

item.title: China's consumer inflation ticks up, outlook for price recovery improves
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's consumer inflation picked up in September, with analysts expecting a gradual recovery in prices to gain traction as improving supply-demand conditions and stronger policy support help bolster domestic demand. The country's consumer price index (CPI), a main gauge of inflation, rose 0.9 percent year on year in September on higher energy and industrial consumer goods prices, according to data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Wednesday. On a monthly basis, the CPI increased 0.2 percent, with the growth rate narrowing by 0.2 percentage points from the previous month. In the first nine months of 2026, consumer prices rose 0.9 percent from a year earlier. The moderate rise reflected improving supply and demand conditions in certain sectors, supported by policies to expand domestic demand and curb excessive competition, noted Liu Fang, an analyst with the National Development and Reform Commission. The year-on-year increase in September was mainly driven by higher energy and industrial consumer goods prices, while falling food prices weighed on overall inflation, NBS statistician Dong Lijuan explained in a statement. Gasoline prices surged 16.6 percent year on year, contributing approximately 0.47 percentage points to the overall CPI increase, the data revealed. Prices of industrial consumer goods, excluding energy, rose 1.6 percent year on year, contributing about 0.39 percentage points to the CPI growth. Service prices increased by 0.8 percent, unchanged from August, contributing around 0.4 percentage points to the CPI increase. Travel-related service prices climbed 2.1 percent, while medical service prices were up by 4 percent. Food prices, meanwhile, fell 1.7 percent year on year, with the decline widening by 0.3 percentage points from August. Pork and fresh vegetable prices fell 10 percent and 8.1 percent respectively, dragging down the overall CPI by approximately 0.33 percentage points. As the country's pork market gradually bottoms out and stabilizes, the downward pressure from pork prices on overall consumer inflation is expected to ease, noted Wen Bin, chief economist at China Minsheng Bank. Meanwhile, increased services consumption during the National Day holiday is expected to provide further support for recovery in core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, Wen said. Wednesday's data also showed China's producer price index (PPI), which measures costs for goods at the factory gate, rose 5 percent year on year in September, with the growth rate accelerating by 1.2 percentage points from August and marking the fastest growth since June 2022. The faster growth was mainly driven by rising international crude oil and non-ferrous metals prices, changes in supply and demand in certain energy and raw material industries, and growing demand from emerging sectors such as artificial intelligence (AI), NBS statistician Dong Lijuan said. The inflation data came as China has rolled out a series of measures to stimulate consumption and strengthen domestic demand, seeking to support economic growth and encourage a reasonable recovery in prices. In July, China released its first five-year plan dedicated exclusively to expanding consumption. The plan aims to unlock the full potential of the country's super-large market, optimize the consumption structure, and improve people's livelihoods through targeted measures. On the monetary front, the People's Bank of China has pledged to make better use of both aggregate and structural monetary policy tools and enhance coordination between monetary and fiscal policies to promote stable economic growth and a reasonable recovery in prices. Looking ahead, positive factors supporting a moderate recovery in prices are expected to continue building as China strengthens countercyclical policy support, advances the development of a unified national market and improves employment and income expectations, helping unlock domestic demand potential, Liu noted. Meanwhile, growing demand from emerging sectors such as AI and continued efforts to curb excessive competition are expected to support prices and improve price transmission. With these factors taking effect, China's overall price levels are expected to remain within a reasonable range for the rest of the year, Liu predicted. ■

item.title: China's energy push set to fuel long-term global energy resilience
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
* China appears to be somewhat shielded from Middle East conflict-driven price shocks by its significant energy reserves, diversified energy supply and rapidly expanding renewable energy sector, which together reduce its dependence on Middle Eastern oil. * China's commitment to and pursuit of peaking carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality before 2060, coupled with rapid advances in wind, solar and new energy vehicle technologies, is fundamentally compressing oil demand. * China's exports of batteries, wind turbines, electric vehicles and, above all, solar panels helped avoid 374 million metric tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions globally in 2025, which is more carbon dioxide emissions than Britain produced last year. BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- As the world confronts what the International Energy Agency (IEA) has described as the most severe energy crisis in its history, China, the world's largest crude importer, has chosen restraint over panic, helping stabilize global oil markets. Rather than scrambling to secure supplies after the Strait of Hormuz, one of the planet's most critical oil choke points, was thrown into turmoil in late February, China has reduced its crude purchases, released strategic reserves to meet domestic needs, and drawn on its increasingly diversified supply channels and expanding renewable energy capacity. The result, according to IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol, has been a meaningful cushion for a market reeling from the largest supply disruption in modern history. On the demand side, China has played an important role in stabilizing markets by reducing its crude oil imports by nearly 50 percent compared with pre-war levels, Birol said in a statement, while noting that significant supplies from Gulf producers and increased exports from the United States, Brazil, Venezuela and Kazakhstan have also helped offset some of the losses from the Gulf. China's restraint has not been accidental. It reflects a viable, multi-layered energy strategy that has been quietly reshaping the country's role in the global energy order: from a passive price-taker vulnerable to geopolitical tremors to an anchor of stability with domestic policy choices now rippling outward, resulting in tangible, positive outcomes for the world economy. OIL PURCHASE RESTRAINT Customs data tell a striking story. In the first nine months of 2026, China's crude oil imports totaled 358 million tonnes, a year-on-year decline of 15.3 percent. This contraction deepened sharply in June, when imports fell to 29.27 million tonnes -- down 41.3 percent from a year earlier and 11.5 percent from May, marking the lowest monthly figure since October 2016. Chen Shouhai, director of the oil and gas policy and law research center at China University of Petroleum in Beijing, anticipates a short-term rebound in imports as restocking demand kicks in during the early stages of any de-escalation, but he cautions that this would represent only a cyclical inventory correction, not a reversal of the underlying demand trend. Over a three-to-five-year horizon, China's total crude imports are likely to decline gradually, according to Chen. The logic is structural, with China's oil consumption having already passed its peak, seeing refined product demand falling year by year since 2024. Petrochemical feedstock demand continues to grow modestly, but nowhere near enough to offset the erosion in transport fuel consumption. Meanwhile, domestic exploration and production have strengthened steadily, with output rising and the import dependency ratio of roughly 70 percent expected to ease. China's commitment to and pursuit of peaking carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality before 2060, coupled with rapid advances in wind, solar and new energy vehicle (NEV) technologies, is fundamentally compressing oil demand. China's decision not to hit the panic button has drawn international attention. Nicholas Wagner, manager of energy initiatives at the World Economic Forum, observed in an analysis of how the war in the Middle East is reshaping Asia's energy transition: "China appears to be somewhat shielded from Middle East conflict-driven price shocks by its significant energy reserves, diversified energy supply and rapidly expanding renewable energy sector, which together reduce its dependence on Middle Eastern oil. This lesson will not be lost on policymakers." STRATEGIC ENERGY PUSH Domestic scholars argue that China's composure amid this global energy tsunami is no accident. It is the product of a strategic architecture first articulated in 2014 -- promoting revolutions in energy consumption, supply, technology and institutions while strengthening international cooperation across the board. Data from the National Energy Administration revealed that in 2025, China's primary energy production had reached 5.13 billion tonnes of standard coal equivalent, with domestic crude oil output hitting 216 million tonnes and natural gas production exceeding 260 billion cubic meters, all record highs. China's energy self-sufficiency rate climbed to 84.4 percent in 2025 and is expected to rise further in 2026. Alongside this domestic expansion, China has constructed a "land-sea linkage, multi-corridor parallel" energy import architecture, with crude oil imported from 49 countries and natural gas from more than 20 countries. Xiao Hongwei, a research fellow at the National Development and Reform Commission, sees the first half of 2026 as a period of multiple breakthroughs in supply security and green transition. China's oil and gas production continued to set records in this period: industrial crude oil output reached 109.43 million tonnes, while natural gas production hit 133 billion cubic meters, both all-time highs for the period. Installed power generation capacity surpassed 4 billion kilowatts, up 10.8 percent year-on-year, maintaining the country's position as the world leader, with non-fossil energy accounting for 62 percent of installed capacity. For the first time, coal-fired power generation fell below 50 percent of total electricity output, while renewable sources exceeded 40 percent, a signal that wind and solar are playing greater roles in China's power mix. Energy efficiency has continued to improve as well. Preliminary calculations show energy consumption grew 2.7 percent in the first half of 2026, with the growth rate decelerating by 1.2 percentage points from the first quarter. Coal's share in the consumption mix held steady, oil's share declined by one percentage point, and clean energy's share rose by one percentage point, serving as evidence that green and low-carbon energy use is becoming an increasingly automatic choice across industries and households. The most visible transformation, however, is in transportation. According to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers, NEV production and sales both exceeded 10.6 million units in the first eight months of 2026, with year-on-year growth of more than 10 percent, while NEVs accounted for 52.4 percent of all new vehicle sales. Zhao Qibo, an economist based in Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in northwest China, said China's long-standing efforts to diversify its energy transport routes, sources and types have clearly paid off. As a stabilizing anchor for national energy security, Xinjiang has abundant oil and coal resources in the traditional energy sector, providing solid support for the country's energy supply. At the same time, Xinjiang's vast land has irreplaceable advantages in wind and solar resources, supplying strong support for sustainable energy development. POTENTIAL BOOST TO WORLD ENERGY FUTURE In June, China released its first-ever five-year plan for building a new energy system, targeting the initial establishment of a clean, low-carbon, safe and efficient energy architecture by 2030. This month, meanwhile, China issued a set of guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces. The energy revolution has been elevated to an unprecedented level, and nuclear power, photovoltaics, energy storage and hydrogen energy have received clear policy endorsement. Hu Ming, Party secretary of China Electric Power Planning and Engineering Institute, describes the coming five years as a period of overlapping security risks and accelerating low-carbon transition. International instability will continue to test the resilience of energy systems, while China's own commitments, including a 17-percent reduction in carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP and a 10-percent decline in energy consumption per unit of GDP, will demand an intensification of the green transition. Under the plan, China will strengthen new energy infrastructure construction, pursue a diversified portfolio spanning wind, solar, hydropower and nuclear power, and expand non-fossil energy supply at scale. This includes steadily advancing coastal nuclear power, offshore wind and distributed new energy development, while actively promoting clean energy bases and transmission corridors in its northern regions and integrated hydro-solar-wind projects in the southwest. Michal Meidan, head of China energy research at the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, argues that the U.S.-Iran conflict has demonstrated the efficacy of China's energy strategy. "China's dependence on imported oil remains substantial, but the geopolitics of energy are shifting from control of oil flows to control of electrified industrial systems," she wrote in a signed article, noting China's clear head start in this transition. Hu also sees the current period as a critical window for speeding up international cooperation in China's energy industry. The present circumstances, he argues, favor leveraging China's industrial strengths in energy technology to expand green industry collaboration and help shape a new pattern of global energy governance. From grid interconnections and clean energy supply chains to technology transfer and joint standards development, opportunities for partnership are expanding just as the global demand for energy resilience has never been more urgent. Lauri Myllyvirta, co-founder of the Helsinki-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, noted that China's exports of batteries, wind turbines, electric vehicles and, above all, solar panels helped avoid 374 million metric tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions globally in 2025, which is more carbon dioxide emissions than Britain produced last year. Calculated over the full lifecycle of these products, China's clean technology exports shipped in 2025 are projected to avoid a total of 6.9 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions over their operating lifetimes. This is a 31-percent increase compared with the 2024 estimate and equivalent to roughly twice India's carbon emissions in 2025, according to the expert. (Video reporter: Su Chuanyi; Video editors: Zhou Yang, Zhao Xiaoqing, Li Qin, Zhang Mocheng and Hong Liang) ■

item.title: Chinese mainland blasts Taiwan authorities' separatist rhetoric regarding history
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday criticized the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities in Taiwan, saying they had unscrupulously distorted history and hyped separatist rhetoric based on a warped version of history. Such rhetoric on history revealed the DPP authorities' true intention of inciting cross-Strait confrontation, said Chen Binhua, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, when responding to a media question on Taiwan authorities' and Lai Ching-te's remarks regarding the history of World War II. It also showed the DPP authorities' ignorance of history and betrayal of the ancestors, Chen said. The Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression was the first to break out and lasted the longest in the World Anti-Fascist War, or World War II, resulting in over 35 million Chinese military and civilian casualties from 1931 to 1945. The victory of the war and the recovery of Taiwan from Japanese occupation are great victories achieved by the Chinese people, including those in Taiwan, at the cost of blood and lives, Chen noted. Taiwan's liberation from the shackles of Japan's colonial rule and its return to the motherland represent an important outcome of the Chinese people's victory in fighting Japanese aggressors, and form an integral part of the post-World War II international order, Chen said. It's a historical memory the Chinese people across the Taiwan Strait should never forget, said Chen, urging compatriots in Taiwan to see the true face of the DPP authorities and stand on the right side of history. Following the Chinese people's victory in the war of resistance against Japanese aggressors, a full-blown civil war broke out between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT). In 1949, the remnants of the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. This unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation, but the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. The real status quo across the Taiwan Strait is that there is only one China in the world and that Taiwan is a part of China, Chen said. By promoting a false narrative of "democracy versus authoritarianism," stoking cross-Strait confrontation, or attempting to pursue "Taiwan independence" through military means and by relying on foreign forces, the DPP authorities will only gradually drag Taiwan into a dangerous situation and bring great disaster to the people in Taiwan, Chen noted. ■

item.title: New bridge linking China, DPRK to facilitate trade, people-to-people exchanges: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- A new bridge across the Yalu River, the border river of China and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), will further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Wednesday. As agreed upon by China and the DPRK, the bridge will officially open to traffic on Thursday, with both sides jointly holding an opening ceremony on that day. China and the DPRK are friendly neighbors connected by mountains and rivers, and the new bridge is an important facility for connectivity between the two countries, Mao said at a regular press briefing. The bridge is expected to boost bilateral trade and people-to-people exchanges, and help improve the well-being of both peoples, she said. ■

item.title: China's yuan loans increase by 11.52 trln yuan in Jan.-Sept. period
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's yuan-denominated loans rose by 11.52 trillion yuan (about 1.71 trillion U.S. dollars) in the first three quarters of 2026, central bank data showed Wednesday. At the end of September, outstanding yuan loans stood at 283.44 trillion yuan, up 4.8 percent year on year, according to the People's Bank of China (PBOC). M2, a broad measure of money supply that covers cash in circulation and all deposits, stood at 359.63 trillion yuan at the end of September, up 7.2 percent year on year. M1, which covers currency in circulation, corporate demand deposits, personal demand deposits and provisions received by non-bank payment institutions, reached 116.76 trillion yuan at the end of September, a rise of 3.2 percent from a year earlier. China's outstanding aggregate financing to the real economy stood at 468.17 trillion yuan at the end of September, up 7.1 percent year on year, according to the central bank. "China's major financial aggregates have maintained reasonable growth, with M2 and aggregate financing to the real economy growing at appropriate rates," said Tian Xuan, dean of Peking University's Guanghua School of Management. "This has helped create a favorable monetary and financial environment for sustained economic improvement." Since the beginning of the year, the PBOC has introduced two rounds of structural monetary policy measures to address the needs of China's transition to new growth drivers and help financial institutions better align their services with the needs of the real economy. The latest round of structural monetary policy measures, announced in September, included cutting the one-year interest rate of the Pledged Supplementary Lending (PSL) facility from 1.75 percent to 1.5 percent, expanding the scope of PSL support, and increasing the quota of the relending facility for sci-tech innovation and technological upgrades by 200 billion yuan. The policy package will channel more funds to areas such as equipment upgrades, strengthen support for sci-tech enterprises, help ease financing constraints on private businesses and reduce their financing costs, said Dong Qingma, deputy head of the Institute of Chinese Financial Studies of Southwestern University of Finance and Economics. The effects of the September policy package are expected to emerge gradually, with existing and new monetary policy measures working in tandem to provide continued support for high-quality development of the real economy, experts said. ■

item.title: China's foreign trade maintains sound momentum as new drivers power exports
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's foreign trade maintained sound momentum in the first three quarters of 2026, with both exports and imports growing rapidly and the overall growth rate reaching its highest level for the same period in five years, official data showed Wednesday. The country's total imports and exports rose 18.8 percent year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan (about 5.94 trillion U.S. dollars) in the January-September period, according to the General Administration of Customs (GAC). Growth accelerated through the year, with the expansion rate rising from 15.3 percent in the first quarter to 18.3 percent in the second quarter and 22.3 percent in the third quarter. Foreign trade growth in the first three quarters was the fastest for the same period in the past five years, with both quarterly and monthly growth rates generally accelerating, said Wang Jun, GAC's deputy head. "Latest international data show that such a growth rate ranks among the top among major economies, and China remains the world's largest trader of goods," the official told a press conference on Wednesday. Wang said the performance could be summed up in four words: "fast, new, quality and open." Describing the "new," he noted that trade in industrial robots, electronic components, computer parts and electrical equipment exceeded 10 trillion yuan in the first three quarters, up 58.9 percent and driving overall import and export growth by 11.3 percentage points. Exports increased 16.4 percent year on year to 23.2 trillion yuan, while imports expanded by 22.3 percent to 16.74 trillion yuan, GAC data showed. In September alone, China's total imports and exports reached 5.16 trillion yuan, up 27.5 percent from a year earlier and crossing the 5-trillion-yuan mark for the first time. This figure also marked the sixth consecutive month of double-digit monthly growth. Exports rose 29.6 percent year on year to 3.03 trillion yuan, while imports grew 24.6 percent to 2.13 trillion yuan for the month. Exports continued to shift toward smarter and greener products. Integrated circuit exports surged 99.1 percent year on year in the first three quarters, while exports of electric vehicles, lithium batteries, and wind power generating sets and their parts rose 72.3 percent, 36.4 percent and 22.4 percent, respectively. In east China's Anhui Province, robotics manufacturer EFORT Intelligent Robot Co., Ltd. has continued to see growth in overseas orders this year. After completing simulated spray-painting tests on vehicle bodies, a batch of its spraying robots will be exported to Italy. The company's overseas revenue increased by more than 50 percent year on year in the first half of 2026. "We provide well-known automakers like Maserati and Volkswagen with integrated robotics solutions for smart production, covering painting, welding, precision assembly and the handling of materials," said You Wei, EFORT's chairman and CEO, adding that EFORT's overseas robot business has grown at a compound annual growth rate of nearly 100 percent over the past three years. Foreign-invested enterprises in China remained active players in the trade expansion. Their total imports and exports rose 19 percent to 11.69 trillion yuan, a record high for the same period, with intermediate goods trade up 27.4 percent to 7.9 trillion yuan and high-tech product exports up 42.1 percent. Wang said more foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains. "The global AI investment boom has kept overseas demand firm, and rising prices will continue to drive rapid growth in chip exports, which is currently the main driver of China's export expansion," said Wang Qing, chief macro analyst at Golden Credit Rating. He added that China's manufacturing upgrading has continued to boost exports of new energy vehicles and high-tech products. The country's trade with more than 180 countries and regions expanded during the first three quarters. Trade with free trade partners reached 19.55 trillion yuan, up 30 percent and contributing over 70 percent of the total trade increment. Meanwhile, trade with other APEC economies rose 23.9 percent to 24.07 trillion yuan. Trade with ASEAN grew 22.7 percent to 6.84 trillion yuan, that with the European Union rose 8.4 percent to 4.78 trillion yuan, and trade with the United States increased 4.1 percent to 3.18 trillion yuan. Exports continued to shift toward new and higher-quality growth drivers. The equipment manufacturing sector contributed nearly 90 percent of the export increment, while intermediate goods accounted for more than half of total exports, underpinning global industrial and supply chains, according to the GAC. ■

item.title: Xi sends congratulatory letter to 140th Canton Fair
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday sent a congratulatory letter to the 140th edition of the China Import and Export Fair, which is also known as the Canton Fair. In his letter, Xi said over the past 70 years since its establishment, the Canton Fair has played a significant role in promoting trade exchanges between China and other countries, serving as an effective platform for China to expand high-level opening up and promote the building of an open world economy. Under the new circumstances, China is willing to join hands with countries around the world to safeguard the multilateral trading system, ensure the stability and smooth operation of global industrial and supply chains, expand the space for mutually beneficial international economic and trade cooperation, and promote a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, to inject new momentum into global development and prosperity, Xi said. The fair opened on the same day in Guangzhou, capital of south China's Guangdong Province. ■
